description:
In this fast-paced, hands-on session hosted by Texas Southern University, you will team up with students from other schools, use a real university research capability, and pair it with an actual Houston problem. With AI tools and live coaching from recruiters and industry leaders, your team will shape a startup idea and pitch it for prizes. No experience, preparation, or STEM background needed.
How it works (90 minutes):
Join a pod (5 min). Sit with 6 to 8 students; your table becomes your team. Your team receives a card describing one Texas Southern research capability, such as flight simulators or drones that map storm damage, and a Houston problem it could help solve.
Hear from the experts (30 min). A panel conversation with leaders in research commercialization, corporate innovation, and startups on how ideas become companies, followed by audience questions.
Build your idea (30 min). Using a simple one-page worksheet, your team decides who has the problem, what you would build, and why it wins. You can use AI tools on your phone to research, and coaches will visit your table.
Pitch (17 min). Every team shares a one-sentence pitch. Judges then pick 4 to 5 finalist teams to give a 60 second pitch on stage and get live feedback.
Win and connect (8 min). Awards in four categories, including a crowd favorite chosen by the room, followed by networking.
What to bring: a charged phone or laptop. Everything else, including the research cards and worksheets, is provided.
Who it serves: This session is designed for career-focused students as well as aspiring founders, emphasizing the skills employers value most: pitching, problem solving, teamwork, and effective use of artificial intelligence.
What you walk away with:
Face time with recruiters and industry leaders who coach and judge your work
Hands-on practice in skills employers want: pitching, problem solving, teamwork, and using AI
Who it serves: Students attending AfroTech U from any college or university. The session is open to all AfroTech U attendees. This session is designed for career-focused students as well as aspiring founders, emphasizing the skills employers value most: pitching, problem solving, teamwork, and effective use of artificial intelligence.
Why it matters: Black founders may lack access to the resources that turn ideas into companies, such as labs, research expertise, data, mentors, and paths to market. Universities, especially HBCUs like Texas Southern, already have many of these resources. This session shows students how to find and use them while they are still in school.

title: Building Fairness Into the Data Supply Chain
speakers: Waverly Rose Brim (Research Engineer, The John's Hopkins University )

speaker_list.name: Waverly Rose Brim
speaker_list.title: Research Engineer
speaker_list.about:
Waverly Rose Brim is an AI research engineer building intelligent systems at the intersection of computer vision, biological foundation models, and surgical data science. Her work focuses on moving machine learning beyond the lab and into clinical environments where reliability, interpretability, and human decision-making matter.

She develops production-grade AI systems that transform patient records, imaging studies, pathology, and clinical guidelines into auditable, decision-ready intelligence for care teams. Her current projects include SCRUB, a surgical computer vision platform designed to track gloved hands in the operating room where conventional pose-estimation models break down; an optimized brain-to-image reconstruction framework capable of running on consumer hardware; and methods for evaluating the safety, fairness, and clinical risk of medical prediction algorithms.

Her earlier work spans multimodal computational pathology and genomics for meningioma characterization, AI-driven surgical skill assessment, operating room analytics, and DARPA-supported neural engineering efforts developing genetically encoded voltage indicators. She has authored more than 20 peer-reviewed publications in medical artificial intelligence and neuro-oncology and previously moderated the “Dr. AI” session at the World Economic Forum's Annual Meeting of the New Champions in Tianjin, China.

Brim is currently pursuing an M.S. in Artificial Intelligence at Johns Hopkins University and is driven by a simple question: How do we build AI systems that clinicians can trust, patients can benefit from, and society can responsibly scale?

description: Bias in clinical AI can begin before training, embedded in decisions about missing data, labels, and success metrics. Waverly Rose Brim explores how strong overall AI model performance can mask harm to Black patients and the underinsured. Through a hands-on, fairness-aware audit workflow using real CDC data, she guides attendees in testing the assumptions built into a clinical pipeline. Together, you’ll examine how upstream modeling choices change who qualifies for treatment and search for hidden harm in overlooked subgroups. You’ll leave with a repeatable audit method and a go/no-go deployment checklist. Bring your laptop to participate. NVIDIA has partnered with Brim to provide complimentary access codes for select NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute courses, helping attendees continue learning beyond the workshop.

description:
A mortgage isn't a document. It's 1.5 million documents a month, nearly a billion data points a year, and a regulatory obligation to be right every time. Every hour of human work in that pipeline gets priced into a fee the buyer pays in cash at closing. Rocket rebuilt origination as a data problem: 10+ petabytes of proprietary data, roughly 70% of monthly documents auto-identified, more than a million team-member hours out of the process.
Then Rocket pointed the same data at the friction before anyone applies the wasted journey. Reaching people when they're genuinely ready cut third-party lead spend 87%. Same data asset. Two kinds of friction. Both priced into what a buyer pays. Papanii Okai, EVP of Engineering, and Kelly Buchanan Spillers, VP of Brand and Product Marketing, walk both halves: where the hours were, what it takes to automate inside a regulated process, why a system that already knows your file feels more human rather than less, and where the savings land. Homeownership is how most families build wealth. The cost of getting in is the gate.

description:

In this role, he leads initiatives in EHR data collection, quality assurance, and system optimization, driving the seamless integration of EHR and real-world data into ASH RC’s Data Hub to power hematologic disease research. His work is central to advancing clinical studies focused on Sickle Cell Disease and Multiple Myeloma.

With deep expertise in health information management and informatics, Travis has implemented EHR systems at scale, conducted interface testing and architecture reviews, and optimized clinical data workflows across platforms, including Cerner Millennium and Epic. He brings advanced technical fluency in HL7 v2, FHIR/JSON, and SQL, enabling robust EHR integration, interoperability, and regulatory compliance. Prior to joining ASH RC, he served as a Health Informatics Subject Matter Expert at Booz Allen Hamilton and as an Interface Architect and EHRM Ambulatory Portfolio Lead at MicroHealth, LLC, where he led cross-functional teams in EHR integration and Meaningful Use attestations.

Travis holds a BS in Biology from Prairie View A&M University and an AAS in Practical Nursing from Lone Star College. He is a Certified ScrumMaster® (CSM®) and holds an Information Privacy and Security (IPS) certification. His rare combination of clinical nursing background, systems architecture expertise, and research informatics leadership gives him a uniquely grounded perspective on the human stakes of the data decisions the health tech industry makes every day.

description: Medical AI is being trained on data that too often leaves Black patients out. Clinical trial participation, representative datasets, and accountable research infrastructure are not optional equity measures. They are the foundation for AI that can accurately diagnose, treat, and save Black lives. With Sickle Cell Disease and Multiple Myeloma as anchors to his argument, Travis Cleaves breaks down how EHR systems and trial pipelines feed medical AI, where Black patients go missing, and what the gap costs.

title: Writing the Next Chapter of Black Prosperity

Frank holds a master’s in integrated marketing communications from Georgetown University and a bachelor’s in advertising management from Michigan State University.

speaker_list.name: Kweli Zukeri
speaker_list.title: Assistant Vice President of Web Innovation and Strategy
speaker_list.about:
Dr. Kweli Zukeri is Assistant Vice President of Web Innovation & Strategy at Howard University, where he has served for over 15 years. He led the development of a centralized web system supporting more than 90 University sites and now advances Howard’s adoption of AI-powered technologies.

A founding member of Howard’s Presidential AI Council, he helps shape responsible AI strategy and governance. His research explores technology, identity, psychological development, and social justice, with a current focus on protecting youth engagement with generative AI while strengthening critical thinking and critical AI literacy.

description:
Every generation inherits a different set of opportunities and obstacles. Ours has inherited one of the greatest technological transformations in modern history. The question is not simply how Black communities participate in this moment, but what we must build to ensure innovation becomes a catalyst for lasting prosperity.
In this thought-provoking conversation, Frank Tramble, Vice President for Communications, Marketing and Public Affairs at Duke University, and Brandon William Jones, Founder and CEO of Gravy Wealth, explore the future of Black prosperity from two connected perspectives: the institutions with the reach and influence to shape opportunity, and the individuals and communities working to turn that opportunity into ownership and generational wealth.
Moderated by Kweli Zukeri, Associate Vice President of Web Innovation & Strategy at Howard University, the discussion will examine how institutional influence, education, capital, and entrepreneurship intersect to shape economic opportunity for Black communities. From expanding access and building trust to developing financial confidence and creating pathways to ownership, the conversation will explore what it takes to move beyond participation in the innovation economy toward building lasting economic power.
Rather than focusing on technology itself, this session challenges attendees to consider the broader ecosystem required to convert today's breakthroughs into tomorrow's generational impact. What responsibility do institutions have to create the conditions for prosperity? How can Black talent and innovation translate into greater ownership? And what decisions must we make today to ensure future generations inherit more than opportunity?
Attendees will leave with a deeper understanding of the relationship between institutional influence and individual economic mobility, practical perspectives on strengthening pathways to ownership, and a renewed sense of their own role in shaping the next chapter of Black prosperity.

Dr. Reginald Parker, President of Freedmen Green Bank & Trust; Jordan Taylor, CEO of SynergyGrid; and Kasheef Wyzard, National Director of Economic Opportunity at Dream.Org, will facilitate a conversation exploring how Community Benefit Agreements, Community Benefit Trusts, and innovative ownership models can transform infrastructure investment into lasting economic opportunity.

title: Financing the Build
speakers: John Payne (CFO, Dream.Org); Noble Madu (Managing Partner and Founder, Plente Group); Ryan Taylor (Innovation Navigator, Bakar Labs for Energy & Materials)

speaker_list.name: John Payne
speaker_list.title: CFO
speaker_list.about: John Payne is Chief Financial Officer of Dream.Org, where he has led financial strategy and operations since 2019. With over 30 years of experience in nonprofit and for-profit financial management, including more than a decade as CFO, John brings expertise in budgeting, accounting, operational efficiency, and financial stewardship. Throughout his career, he has overseen operating budgets totaling $55 million and capital expenditure budgets totaling $5 million. He studied finance at San Diego State University and has led financial operations for organizations across the Bay Area since 1996.

speaker_list.name: Noble Madu
speaker_list.title: Managing Partner and Founder
speaker_list.about: Noble Madu is Founder & Managing Partner of Plente Group, a recruiting technology company that enables recruiters, hirers and well-connected people to facilitate leadership hiring. Plente has represented more than $100 million in annual compensation since 2020. He is also a Partner at CSP, an affiliated executive search firm advising leading investment firms & businesses on critical leadership hires. Noble brings 15 years of experience as a private equity investor, executive search professional & entrepreneur, including roles focused on business and investment growth at Goldman Sachs, Korn Ferry, Bay Mountain Capital, & Skystream Technology.

speaker_list.name: Ryan Taylor
speaker_list.title: Innovation Navigator
speaker_list.about: Ryan Taylor is a climate technology investor and energy finance professional with over a decade of experience advancing clean energy innovation. His career spans early-stage venture capital, utility-scale renewable energy project finance, and technology consulting. He has supported investments in breakthrough technologies and the development of solar and wind projects, bringing expertise in commercialization, capital deployment, and energy infrastructure. Ryan holds a BS in Chemical Physics from UC Davis and is pursuing an MS in Systems Engineering at Johns Hopkins University

description:
Great ideas don't build infrastructure. Aligned capital, capable partners, and clear pathways to implementation do. How do cities move promising solutions beyond pilots and into financeable, scalable projects that deliver lasting community value?
Join Ryan Taylor, climate technology investor and energy finance expert, and Noble Madu, Partner at Plente Group, with John Payne, Chief Financial Officer at Dream.Org, moderating.
Drawing on experience across utility-scale renewable energy, venture capital, investment management, and institutional partnerships, panelists will explore how public, private, and philanthropic capital can work together to accelerate infrastructure development. From project finance and commercialization to value capture and access to capital, the conversation examines the financial structures, strategic relationships, and investment opportunities needed to move from concept to construction—while ensuring economic returns translate into meaningful benefits for communities.

title: Resilience Hubs & Emergency Comms
speakers: Nneka Uzoh Kibuule (Founder and CEO, Kino Cove); Sequoia Riley (Independent Climate Consultant, N/A); Jasmine Davenport (Vice President of Program Strategy, Dream.Org); Chantel Greene (Chief of Tribal Relations, UnityCloud; Founder and CEO, Xexus Greene Energy, UnityCloud; Xexus Greene Energy)

speaker_list.name: Nneka Uzoh Kibuule
speaker_list.title: Founder and CEO
speaker_list.about: Nneka Kibuule is the founder and CEO of Kino Cove, a household resilience platform built for institutions and designed for families. She brings 17 years of experience in climate finance and clean energy, with roles at NextEra, PG&E, Elemental Impact, and Aligned Climate Capital. Her work on the 2018 Camp Fire response shaped her understanding of how disasters affect communities. She holds finance degrees from Tulane and Hampton and an MBA from Kellogg. She lives in Oakland with her family and loves gardening.

speaker_list.name: Sequoia Riley
speaker_list.title: Independent Climate Consultant
speaker_list.about: Dr. Sequoia Riley is an urban and regional planning researcher with over nine years of experience in research, data analysis, and program management. She has led more than 15 climate adaptation projects, advancing green infrastructure across urban and rural communities. With a PhD in Urban and Regional Planning, she focuses on practical climate adaptation and resilience solutions for underserved communities, collaborating with community partners, government agencies, and funders.

speaker_list.name: Jasmine Davenport
speaker_list.title: Vice President of Program Strategy
speaker_list.about: Jasmine Davenport is a climate scientist, strategist, and advocate from Monroe, Louisiana, and recipient of the 2022 JFK New Frontier Award for her climate justice work. She previously served as Senior Advisor for Climate Justice in the Biden-Harris Administration, advising on $11 billion in Inflation Reduction Act funding. As Executive Director of Our Climate, she helped mobilize over 10,000 young people to advocate for equitable climate policies. She holds a master’s degree in Tropical Marine Biology from the University of Essex.

speaker_list.name: Chantel Greene
speaker_list.title: Chief of Tribal Relations, UnityCloud; Founder and CEO, Xexus Greene Energy
speaker_list.about: Chantel Greene, a Nez Perce Tribal member, is Chief of Tribal Relations at UnityCloud, Founder and CEO of Xexus Greene Energy, and President of Sidney Resource Corporation. She served as Vice-Chairwoman of the Nez Perce Tribal Council (2018–2021). A GRID Alternatives Tribal Energy Innovators Fellow, she completed the Tribe’s solar and storage resiliency project featuring Idaho’s first Tribal Tesla Megapacks, with service learning and workforce development for Tribal members. She holds a Master of Legal Studies in Indigenous Peoples Law from the University of Oklahoma

description: When disruptions strike, resilience hubs help communities access critical services, connect with loved ones, and maintain stability. Join Nneka Uzoh Kibuule, Founder and CEO of Kino Cove; Dr. Sequoia Riley, Independent Climate Consultant; and Chantel Greene, Chief of Tribal Relations at UnityCloud and Founder and CEO of Xexus Greene Energy, with moderator Jasmine Davenport, Dream.Org’s VP of Program Strategy. Together, they will explore how household preparedness, green infrastructure, Tribal-led solar and storage, and community partnerships strengthen climate adaptation, emergency communications, and continuity of essential services

title: OURstory, NOT HIStory
speakers: Sean Wilson (National Director of Organizing and Partnerships, Dream.Org); J Paul Johnson (Founder, BlackEverything.com); Michael Hawthorne Jr (Co-Founder, Klean Energy Entertainment)

speaker_list.name: Sean Wilson
speaker_list.title: National Director of Organizing and Partnerships
speaker_list.about: Sean Wilson is the National Director of Organizing and Partnerships at Dream.Org, advancing leadership, strategic partnerships, and economic opportunity. Raised in Milwaukee's 53206 neighborhood, Sean spent 17 years incarcerated before becoming a national leader in organizing and systems change. He has developed leadership programs spanning more than 35 states, empowering justice-impacted communities to influence policy and access opportunity. His work includes engagements with the United Nations and a feature in HBO's "Growing Up Milwaukee." Sean believes those closest to systemic challenges must help shape the future.

speaker_list.name: J Paul Johnson
speaker_list.title: Founder
speaker_list.about: J. Paul Johnson is an entrepreneur, economist, and Founder of BlackEverything.com, a digital ecosystem preserving Black culture, history, commerce, and intellectual capital. A Texas Southern University graduate, he previously served as Vice President at Chase Bank, Chief Operating Officer of a Houston school district, and Chairman of Texas Southern University's Board of Regents. His work bridges finance, technology, and community development to advance cultural preservation, economic opportunity, and collective ownership. Johnson is committed to helping Black communities own their stories and build generational wealth.

speaker_list.name: Michael Hawthorne Jr
speaker_list.title: Co-Founder
speaker_list.about: Michael Hawthorne Jr. is Co-Founder of Klean Energy Kulture, CEO of Electric Kulture, and Head of Planning for Atlanta Climate Week. An environmentalist, climate justice advocate, and cultural innovator, he bridges clean energy, entertainment, and community engagement to make climate action accessible and relevant. His career includes work with Greenpeace, the Sierra Club's Beyond Coal campaign, and national environmental initiatives. Through Klean Energy Kulture, Michael leverages music, storytelling, and pop culture to amplify underrepresented voices, accelerate clean energy adoption, and build a more inclusive climate economy.

description:
Who tells a community's story shapes who gets to define its future. As cities evolve through technological innovation, infrastructure investment, and economic development, whose voices are shaping the vision—and whose stories are being left behind?
Join J Paul Johnson, Founder of BlackEverything.com, and Michael Hawthorne Jr., Co-Founder of Klean Energy Kulture, with Sean Wilson, National Director of Organizing and Partnerships at Dream.Org, moderating.
Together, they'll explore storytelling as essential infrastructure—a tool for preserving community history, elevating lived experience, building collective power, and influencing how cities invest and grow. From cultural preservation and climate storytelling to community organizing and economic opportunity, this conversation examines how residents can move beyond being subjects of change to becoming authors of their communities' futures.
Because building smarter cities isn't just about what we build. It's about whose stories, voices, and visions guide the way.

speaker_list.title: Author, Entrepreneur, and Voting Rights Activist

speaker_list.name: Brooklyn Williams

description: Entrepreneur, political leader, and bestselling author Stacey Abrams on Coded Justice, her Avery Keene thriller set inside a tech company building an AI system poised to revolutionize healthcare. Drawing on her experience co-founding multiple companies and leading in politics, she explores what happens when billions of dollars, a charismatic founder, and a fast-moving technology collide, and the moral boundaries that should govern what we build.

title: Turning Internal Expertise Into AI-Proof Personal Brands
location: Product & Innovation Stage (Exhibit Hall C&D (1st Floor))
speakers: Roxy Couse (Founder, Sloefy)

speaker_list.name: Roxy Couse
speaker_list.title: Founder
speaker_list.about:
Roxy Couse is the founder of Sloefy, a personal branding platform for corporate professionals who want to build public influence without compromising their careers.  She is a digital storyteller and expert voice in corporate culture recognized for her wildly relatable millennial manager skits that captures the unspoken reality of work life with humor, honesty, and authority. 

 She is also a Webby Nominated Creator and has partnered with brands like LinkedIn, Anthropic, IBM, The Project Management Institute, P & G, CVS, Amazon, and more.

description: Layoffs in tech hit Black workers first and hardest. AI is accelerating that curve. Meanwhile, the professionals landing board seats, advisor roles, and next jobs before the old one ends all share one thing — a public personal brand they built while still employed. But Black corporate professionals are navigating landmines their peers aren't. Compliance reviews that hit harder. HR policies enforced selectively. The respectability tax. The real, rational fear of retaliation for speaking publicly about work. Roxy built Sloefy — a personal branding platform for corporate professionals — because she lived this. In this session she will walk through the Personal Brand Map framework she uses with clients, show attendees how to extract workplace expertise without crossing compliance lines, and leave them with a 30-day plan they can start Monday morning. This is not a "build your personal brand" talk. It's a leverage strategy for a workforce that needs one before the layoff email arrives.

title: The Video Backlog: Leveraging AI to Produce More with Descript
location: Product & Innovation Stage (Exhibit Hall C&D (1st Floor))
speakers: Marcello Farrell (Sales Engineer, Descript)

speaker_list.name: Marcello Farrell
speaker_list.title: Sales Engineer
speaker_list.about:
Marcello Farrell is a Sales Engineer at Descript, where he helps creators, marketers, and media teams fit the software to the actual work of making something worth listening to.

Outside Descript, Marcello is an Audio Engineer and gigging drummer with years under his belt in both. He spent years making visual work in the greater St. Louis glitch art scene, all while while drumming, managing, and recording local bands and artists across genres such as pop, rock, r&b, rap, and alternative.

description:
Every team is being asked for more video: marketing, training, internal comms, exec thought leadership, and beyond. The requests keep growing, but the production team doesn't, and most of the work sits in a backlog.
In this hands-on session we’ll take a rough recording to a finished video in real time. Attendees will learn the AI tools in Descript that handle the polish that used to require a professional editor, then use Underlord, Descript's AI co-editor, to apply that same work across a whole project from written prompts. You give the creative direction. The AI does the edits.
Attendees will leave with a repeatable process they can run themselves or hand to their team.

title: Pilot to Profit Innovation Showcase
speakers: Kasheef Wyzard (National Director of Economic Opportunity, Dream.Org); Reginald Parker (CEO, Green Power Ventures)

speaker_list.name: Kasheef Wyzard
speaker_list.title: National Director of Economic Opportunity
speaker_list.about: Kasheef Wyzard is the National Director of Economic Opportunity at Dream.Org, leading initiatives that advance workforce development, entrepreneurship, and an inclusive green economy. His work has reached over 1,000 participants, deployed $2M in scholarships, invested $1.3M in underrepresented founders, and mobilized $5.3M in catalytic capital. A Georgia State University graduate and member of Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity, Inc., Kasheef believes those closest to the problem must help lead the solutions.

speaker_list.name: Reginald Parker
speaker_list.title: CEO
speaker_list.about: Dr. Reginald Parker is President of Freedmen Green Bank & Trust, Managing Partner of Green Power Ventures, and President of Optimal Technology Corporation. With over 25 years of experience in engineering, clean energy, and technology commercialization, he has developed more than 15 clean energy and manufacturing technologies and commercialized over $60 million in new products. A former university professor and BCG consultant, Dr. Parker focuses on advancing renewable energy, climate resilience, and economic opportunity in underserved communities. He holds degrees from MIT, Georgia Tech, and Florida State University.

description:
Cities don't just need more innovation. They need solutions they can deploy. What does it take to move promising technologies beyond the pilot stage and into real municipal contracts, commercial opportunities, and community impact?
Join Kasheef Wyzard, National Director of Economic Opportunity at Dream.Org, and Dr. Reginald Parker, President of Freedmen Green Bank & Trust, as they facilitate the culmination of the Pilot to Profit accelerator.
This showcase features founders developing solutions aligned with real municipal challenges—from energy and infrastructure to resilience, housing, and community well-being. Through direct feedback, strategic connections, and engagement with potential buyers and partners, founders are on a journey to adoption, investment, and scale.
Because the goal isn't simply to showcase what's possible. It's to turn innovation into implementation—and create economic opportunity in the process.
